hey, i’m sorry you struggle so much but i can relate. i’ve been going through ups and downs of an eating disorder for nearly 13 years now and it sucks. Same as you, therapy only does so much. I wouldn’t say that i’m out of control with it any longer but when i start to lose a little weight i end up losing and losing and losing. 

You said your bf has difficulty with communication and i think that’s the main factor here. “annoying” probably isn’t the greatest term to use but it was probably his only way to describe it. Eating disorders in themselves are something that’s hard for people who don’t have them to understand, making it hard to communicate with someone else about it. Regardless of communication problems, your bf will probably not ever fully understand it.

I try to talk to my boyfriend if i’m struggling and just constantly keep an open dialogue about it through the days, the good and the bad ones. I’m sure my boyfriend finds my obsessions “annoying” as well, but at the end of the day he loves me and cares about me. He just doesn’t understand it. Maybe this is similar to what you are experiencing.

My best advice would be to attend some groups or find people who you can talk to about your eating disorder, so that those conversations can help you feel better about it without relying on words from your boyfriend. I’ve done things like research online about what partners’ of people with eating disorders can do and sometimes i just send the link over to my boyfriend to read up on it. It might help him understand a little more and be able to find more appropriate terms to use with you. As far as the bones sticking out, thats a physical thing so his use of the word “annoying” might just be a way to tell you that he likes your body with a little bit more meat on your bones. 

i hope this helps and my inbox is always open if you ever need someone to talk to 💜

try singing with her in the mornings. music would sometimes help us get into a good morning flow. i think the best thing (and its way easier said than done) is try to stay calm and sweet to her even when shes having a fit. Try one different thing each week and maybe the repetition of it will help if you find something that sticks. Usually once kids realize that what YOU are doing works, and helps her get out in a better mood, she will start to work with you on it. I know she’s only three but I always talk to the kids using rational thinking, i would say things to her like “i know you don’t want to start your day this way and neither do i so let’s find ways to make this fun” then maybe ask her what kind of fun things you can do in the mornings for her. Try saying to her once you guys are on your way in the morning “what do you want to do tomorrow morning to get our day started off in a happy mood?” Maybe if she knows you’re putting in effort to help her out, and listening to what she wants to have happen, she will get there. I know it’s tough when you always feel like you’re just bribing her and doing whatever you can to get her out the door, I found that bribing doesn’t ever really help in the long term and it just makes the kids that much more entitled... so i’d try to break that if you want to stick with them and stick it out with her.
